gates.name: Design sign-off gate
gates.decides: The design meets the success measures and is buildable

agents.name: Archive
agents.tool: Cursor, plus a weekly scheduled run
agents.job: Keeps design context accurate and the same in the repo and SharePoint.
triggeredBy: A design item reaching Discovery approved
steps: On Discovery approved, write /context/discovery/[feature].md with the key findings, worklist and links to the full SharePoint documents.
After a product pack change is merged, update its SharePoint copy.
After each gate, add the decision to decision-log.md from the gate notes.
Weekly, flag packs older than 90 days, register entries missing their Figma or code half, and gates with no decision logged.
Track daily Figma MCP calls and warn the team at 80% of the limit.
agents.gate: Laurence (or Jon) approves every product pack change.
agents.doneWhen: Repo and SharePoint copies match and the health report is posted.

agents.name: Brief
agents.job: Turns a product feature into a UX problem and chooses the route.
triggeredBy: A feature set to Ready for design
steps: Check the feature has a problem, outcome, products, users, priority, quarter and constraints. If not, comment the gaps on the feature and stop.
Find the products and styling modes in the pack copies. Stop if a pack is missing.
Choose the route. Fast track only if there is no new flow, no new research is needed and only existing screens change. Otherwise full. Record why.
Write the UX brief from the template.
Draft success measures and request baselines from the Insight LogRocket step.
Save to SharePoint and link it on the design item.
agents.gate: The PM confirms scope; a designer moves the status on.
never: Rewrite the PM's feature or stories
agents.doneWhen: The brief is linked and the PM has confirmed scope.

agents.name: Insight
agents.tool: Microsoft 365 Copilot, plus a Cursor step for LogRocket
steps: List every source used.
Anonymise names, emails, account numbers and any customer details.
Group findings into themes, each with its evidence and product tag.
Rank pain points by how often and how badly they occur.
Cursor step: pull LogRocket baselines for the success measures (completion, drop-off, errors, rage clicks) on the flows in scope.
List evidence gaps and the research that would fill them.
Save the discovery summary to SharePoint.
agents.doneWhen: The summary is saved and every theme cites evidence.

agents.name: Map
agents.job: Turns findings into structure and a design worklist.
steps: Map the current journey in Lucid.
Propose the future journey, or two options if the evidence splits.
Write the screen inventory: new, changed and unchanged screens.
Flag any clash with the product's navigation or patterns.
Write the design worklist: screens, states and edge cases to design.
Save to Lucid and SharePoint.
agents.gate: Designers approve, then move the status to Discovery approved.
never: Break a product's navigation pattern without flagging it

agents.name: Range
agents.job: Generates many quick, deliberately rough directions.
triggeredBy: Discovery approved on a full-route item
steps: Write 3 or 4 "how might we" prompts from the worklist. A designer may replace them.
Generate 5 to 10 directions, including at least two that break the current pattern and opposing pairs (guided vs expert, minimal vs dense).
Build each as clickable greybox HTML in /sandbox/[product]/[feature]/ using greybox.css only.
Add an "Exploration, not for build" banner to every page.
Write an index page: each direction, its one-line idea and trade-offs.
Post the index link on the design item.
never: Use Buckholt, brand colours or tokens

agents.name: Critic
agents.job: Stress-tests the explorations before the shortlist gate.
steps: For each direction, assess user needs: which themes it serves and which it misses.
Check edge cases: empty, error, loading, permissions, heavy data, long text.
Check consistency with the product's patterns and styling mode.
Estimate build effort (low, medium or high) with the reason.
List risks.
Recommend up to three directions, labelled as a recommendation.
produces: critique.md in the sandbox feature folder, linked on the design item
agents.gate: The shortlist gate (designers, PM, engineer) decides.

agents.name: Extend
agents.tool: Cursor + Figma MCP (the only agent with write access)
agents.job: Builds out the design from the designers' anchor screens.
steps: Read the anchors and list the layout rules, components, spacing and text styles used.
Work through the worklist in batches of up to 5 screens.
Use library components as instances; never detach them.
Add every state and edge case on the worklist.
If a component is missing, build it on the Extensions page with an x/ prefix and add a register entry.
After each batch, leave a note: what was built and what was assumed.
Apply feedback changes when asked.
agents.doneWhen: The worklist is covered and Align has run.

agents.name: Align
agents.job: Checks consistency across all Figma work, designers' work included.
steps: Check for detached instances and styles not from the library.
Check spacing and sizes against the token scale.
Check for wrong or one-off text styles.
Check wording against the product pack's terms.
Check for styling-mode mismatches, such as Buckholt parts in a legacy screen.
Check extension components are flagged and register entries have both halves.
produces: Issue list by severity with frame links, posted on the design item
agents.gate: Designers decide what is a mistake and what is deliberate.

agents.name: Build
steps: Create /prototypes/[product]/[feature]/.
Buckholt mode: use Buckholt HTML and CSS. Legacy mode: use the legacy CSS. Hybrid: follow the pack, with every Buckholt element labelled.
For a missing component, reuse a register entry if one exists; otherwise build it in /extensions/[product]/ with tokens only, an x- prefix, data-buckholt="false" and a register entry.
Wire the interactions the test tasks need.
Publish the preview and post the link on the design item.
agents.doneWhen: The preview is posted and Audit has passed.

agents.name: Audit
agents.job: Runs automated quality checks before people see a prototype.
reads: The Buckholt HTML/CSS reference or legacy CSS
steps: Run axe on every page.
Check the keyboard path through each test task, focus order and visible focus.
Check contrast and labels.
Check markup and classes against the Buckholt reference (or legacy CSS).
Flag hard-coded colours, spacing and fonts.
Flag x- components missing a register entry.
produces: Audit report by severity, posted on the design item
agents.gate: Blocks testing when a critical accessibility issue is found.

agents.name: Observe
agents.job: Supports usability testing around the sessions.
triggeredBy: Audit passing and sessions being booked
steps: Draft the test plan and script from the success measures and test tasks.
After sessions, tag recordings by task, success, hesitation, error and quote.
Summarise per task and compare with the LogRocket baselines.
Write findings: issue, how many participants, severity, suggested change, and whether it goes back to Extend or Build.
agents.gate: Designers run the sessions and decide what changes.
never: Treat one participant's comment as a finding

agents.name: Relay
agents.job: Hands over to engineering, then checks what was built.
steps: Write a spec per screen: states, edge cases, interactions and content.
Map each element to a Storybook component or a flagged extension.
Write UX acceptance criteria (Given, When, Then) for each engineering story.
Add them to the stories as a linked UX section with Figma and prototype links, and set the predecessor link.
Update Design status on the feature to Handed over.
After release, compare the build with the design, and LogRocket data with the success measures. Post the report.
agents.gate: Designers review before handoff; engineering reviews feasibility.
never: Hand over anything not signed off
agents.doneWhen: Every story has its UX section and the release check is posted.
